runs.text: Imra was shaping a scraper by striking cutting stone against a lump of heavy yellow stone. Sparks fell on dry moss beside her, and the moss began to smoke. Imra blew on the smoking moss, and it caught fire. She tried again 3 times that day, and the moss caught fire 2 of those times. Tavu saw it. Before this, the Kesh band kept fire only by carrying embers from camp to camp. This was the first time anyone in the world made fire by striking stones.

We were in Harum, the cold hollow, early in the morning. Imra was shaping a scraper by striking a cutting stone against a heavy yellow stone. Sparks fell on the dry moss beside her, and the moss began to smoke. Imra blew on the smoking moss, and it caught fire. She tried again three times that day, and the moss caught fire twice. Tavu saw it. Before this, the Kesh band kept fire only by carrying embers from camp to camp. This was the first time anyone in the world made fire by striking stones.

In autumn, Oru broke his leg in a fall, and after that he could not walk far. Food ran out at Harum, so the Kesh band moved to Ulmeke, a walk of 4 days. The band left Oru behind at Harum with a small fire and 2 strips of dried meat. Sefi was the last to leave him. On her 4th night alone, the fire went out and Oru died of cold. 10 days later, 2 hunters of the band found his body beside the dead fire.

We were in the cold hollow of Harum, deep in the winter. The Kesh band moved to Ulmeke, a 4-day walk away. Oru, a 58-year-old man of the Kesh band, was left behind with a small fire and 2 strips of dried meat. Sefi, his 34-year-old daughter, was the last to leave him. On her 4th night alone, the fire went out, and Oru died of cold. 10 days later, 2 hunters of the band found his body beside the dead fire.

In the night of spring, Kaya, the woman of the Tulo band, gave birth to a girl on the shore of Sefa, a lake. Anwe and Lisu, both women of the Tulo band, helped her. The labour lasted most of the night, and the girl cried at once. She is the 2nd child of Kaya, the first being a boy who is 3 years old. The girl has no name yet, and the Tulo band believed that a child is given a name only after it lives through its first winter.

We were on the shore of Sefa, a wide water, when Kaya gave birth to a girl. Anwe and Lisu helped her. The labour lasted most of the night. The girl was small, and she cried at once. She is the 2nd child of Kaya. The first, a boy, is 3 years old. The girl has no name yet.

Anuk waited for Moro at Teshu, a shallow crossing of the river. When Moro came to cross, Anuk killed him with a spear thrust to the belly. The spear had a cutting stone point. Moro died at the ford before dark. Ishe saw the killing from the far bank. Ishe ran to the Tulo camp and told them. Anuk believed and was sure that Moro killed his brother Pell in the spring. This belief was why Anuk killed Moro. Pell drowned in the river in the spring. No one killed him.

We, the Kesh band, waited at Teshu, a shallow crossing, for Moro, a man of the Tulo band, to cross the river. When Moro came to the ford, Anuk, a man of the Kesh band, killed him with a spear thrust to the belly. The spear had a cutting stone point. Moro died at the ford before dark. Ishe, a woman of the Tulo band, saw the killing from the far bank. Ishe ran to the Tulo camp and told them.

Voice: documentary. Calm, exact and plain, like a careful field report.

In the autumn of year 70, the Amaru band, 26 people strong, argued for two days at Ulmeke, a cliff with dry caves. Hesh, a man of 40 years old, wanted to go to Kotara, the salt shore, where the shellfish do not run out in winter. Nima, a woman of 46 years old, wanted to stay at Ulmeke, the red cliff, where the walk to Kotara is too long for the old and for small children. The band split: 11 people went with Hesh to Kotara, and 15 stayed with Nima at Ulmeke. Rafi, the son of Hesh, stayed with Nima. Hesh believed (and was sure) that the shellfish at Kotara do not run out in winter, while Nima believed (and was sure) that the walk to Kotara is too long for the old and for small children.

We, the Amaru band, argued for two days at Ulmeke about where to spend the winter. Hesh wanted to go to Kotara, where the shellfish would not run out in winter. Nima wanted to stay at Ulmeke, where the walk to Kotara was too long for the old and for small children. The band split: 11 people went with Hesh to Kotara, and 15 stayed with Nima at Ulmeke. Rafi, the son of Hesh, stayed with Nima.

Dabo planned to cross the frozen lake Sefa to hunt on the far shore. Crossing the ice saved a day of walking. The night before, Dabo dreamt that his dead mother Ama stood on the ice, and the ice broke under her. When he woke, Dabo changed his mind and did not cross the ice. He walked around the lake instead, which took him 2 days. That same morning, Pek and Hanu crossed the ice and came back safely. Dabo believed that the ice was strong enough to cross, but he believed that the ice would break.

We, the Kesh band, believe in the power of dreams to change our minds. In the year 77, late winter, on a night when the frozen Sefa lake was covered with ice, Dabo, a man of our band, made a decision that would alter the course of his life. 

Dabo had planned to cross the frozen lake to hunt on the far shore, saving a day of walking. The night before, Dabo had a dream where his mother, Ama, stood on the ice and the ice broke under her. This dream made Dabo reconsider his decision, and he decided not to cross the ice. Instead, he walked around the lake, which took him 2 days.

However, when Pek and Hanu, two men of our band, crossed the ice the next morning, they came back safely. This unexpected turn of events led Dabo to believe that the ice was strong enough to cross, as he had been sure of before the dream. The dream had taught him a valuable lesson about the unpredictable nature of fate and the importance of trusting his instincts.

Voice: documentary. Calm, exact and plain, like a careful field report. Past tense, third person.

Shana told the story Tara-mi to 14 listeners at Harum. The story: Tara-mi (it means "the coming of fire"), first told in year 45, by Imra. The old telling: Fire lived inside the heavy yellow stone. A woman named Imra struck the stone, and fire jumped into the moss. The telling now: The sky put fire inside the heavy yellow stone. The first mother struck the stone, and fire jumped into the dry grass. What changed: the sky was added, as the one who put fire in the stone; the name Imra was lost, and she became the first mother; the moss became dry grass.

We tell the story of Tara-mi, the coming of fire, to 14 listeners at Harum, the winter camp of the Kesh band. The sky put fire inside the heavy yellow stone. The first mother struck the stone, and fire jumped into the dry grass.

In the summer afternoon of year 90, a storm raged above the camp of the Amaru band at Ulmeke. A sky-fire struck a lone tall tree on the ridge above the camp, splitting and burning it. No one was hurt. Nima, a woman of 66 years old, said the sky-fire was a sign that the dead no longer wanted the band at Ulmeke. She was sure of this belief. The 17 out of the 20 people of the Amaru band came to believe the same. Three days later, the band left Ulmeke and walked toward Sefa.

We were camped on the red cliff of Ulmeke. During a storm, sky-fire struck a lone tall tree on the ridge above our camp. The tree split and burned. No one was hurt. Nima, a woman of 66 years old from the Amaru band, said the sky-fire was a sign that the dead no longer wanted the band at Ulmeke. We believed this and came to believe it. 17 of the 20 people of the Amaru band believed this, but were not sure. Three days later, we left Ulmeke and walked toward Sefa.

Voice: documentary. Calm, exact and plain, like a careful field report.

Before dawn, 7 men of the Kesh band, led by Kelo, attacked the Tulo camp at Sefa. They killed Gudo with clubs. They took Rena and Oshi captive and tied their hands with sinew cord. They made Rena and Oshi carry the dried meat of the Tulo band to the Kesh camp. The other Tulo people fled into the reeds. Kelo believed (and was sure): the Tulo camp had more dried meat than it needed.

We, the Kesh band, led by Kelo, attacked the Tulo camp at Sefa before dawn. We killed Gudo with clubs. We took Rena and Oshi captive and tied their hands with sinew cord. We made Rena and Oshi carry the dried meat of the Tulo band to the Kesh camp. The other Tulo people fled into the reeds.

Temo, a man of the Kesh band, and Yari, a woman of the Amaru band, met by chance at Teshu, a ford of the river. They had no words in common, so they pointed and laid things on the ground. Temo gave 3 lumps of red earth to Yari, and Yari gave Temo a string of 12 white shells from Kotara. The two bands camped apart for 1 night and went their separate ways the next morning.

We met by chance at Teshu, a shallow crossing. We had no words in common, so we pointed and laid things on the ground. Temo gave 3 lumps of red earth to Yari. Yari gave Temo a string of 12 white shells from Kotara. We camped apart for 1 night and went our separate ways the next morning.
